text:
jess-partnerships: Heads up — Atlas Systems' procurement put the marketplace purchase on hold. Their PO portal rejects our upload with 'sellerMismatch' error. Need legal + procurement help. @lee @dan
lee-procurement: on it. Any error payload? can we get the exact file they tried to upload?
jess-partnerships: they attached a portal screenshot in email. main issue: Atlas wants the partner of record to be 'Atlas Systems Services LLC' and expects Redwood to be listed as a line-item vendor. The marketplace requires vendor==seller, so their transform fails.
dan-legal: that's a contract/commerce mismatch. We can't be listed as the seller under their name. Can Atlas accept Redwood invoicing them instead? Need the PO PDF and the XML they push to the marketplace gateway.
olivia-ops: cc @atlas-sys-poc-bot can you paste the XML fragment they submit and which marketplace (aws/azure/gcp)?
atlas-sys-poc-bot: Upload metadata: marketplace=azure, id=AZ-PO-99877, error='sellerMismatch'. XML fragment: `<SellerName>Atlas Systems Services LLC</SellerName><Vendor>Redwood Inference Inc.</Vendor>`
lee-procurement: Azure marketplace enforces that the seller in the PO matches the publisher account. If Atlas insists on being seller, we'd need them to be a registered publisher or for us to list them as a reseller under our publisher — both require marketplace agreements we don't have in place.
jess-partnerships: Atlas expected a drop-ship style flow where they appear as buyer/seller in their internal system and Redwood shows up only on invoice lines. They say their internal compliance won't accept anything else. @dan any legal workaround short-term?
dan-legal: We can do pass-through invoicing (Redwood invoices Atlas, Atlas invoices the end-customer) but need a signed addendum shifting payment routing and clarifying indemnities/tax handling. Not instantaneous.
olivia-ops: Short-term ops workaround: accept Atlas' PO via email to partnerships@ and handle the order manually in our billing system to match their PO number. That bypasses the marketplace portal but will require manual reconciliation.
lee-procurement: Finance will push back — marketplace reconciliation and usage-based billing from Azure won't align with a manual entry. This could create duplicate billing unless we coordinate closely with Azure and Atlas.
jess-partnerships: Atlas is pushing for pilot go-live next week (high-visibility SI reference). Is there an escalation with Azure to allow a reseller override for this one case?
dan-legal: I'll draft a limited addendum that allows pass-through billing for this specific customer with audit rights. Timebox: 72 hours to get countersignature from Atlas. Need Atlas legal contact and DUNS/VAT info.
atlas-sys-poc-bot: Atlas legal contact: m.singh@atlassys.com. VAT: EU-AT-GB12345. They say they're willing to sign an addendum that names Redwood as 'Subcontractor' on the internal PO.
lee-procurement: DUNS/VAT/W9-equivalent — procurement can provide. Subcontractor label seems workable on our side pending legal approval. But again, marketplace portal validation will still fail if seller != publisher.
dan-legal: Proposed operational approach: 1) Atlas issues an internal PO that names Redwood as Subcontractor. 2) Redwood submits the marketplace purchase under our publisher account so the Azure flow succeeds. 3) Redwood invoices Atlas for the purchase (pass-through). That keeps Azure happy and meets Atlas' internal controls. Need Atlas sign-off on reconciliation approach.
olivia-ops: Practical questions: do we have authority to submit the marketplace purchase under our account for Atlas, or does Atlas require the purchase under their tenant?
jess-partnerships: Atlas says they need the purchase reflected in their internal procurement system as coming from their legal entity. They can accept a separate internal PO for services that references the marketplace invoice number.
sarah-sales: Approved this route for the pilot. We'll accept 30-day terms and a short SOW to cover responsibilities.
marco-finance: Quick finance Q: who collects VAT and how? If Atlas is EU-registered and wants reverse charge, we need their VAT ID on file. Also need clear payment terms before invoicing.
atlas-sys-poc-bot: Confirmed VAT ID: EU-AT-GB12345. Atlas requests Redwood not to charge VAT (reverse charge).
lee-procurement: We'll collect DUNS and VAT docs and pass to legal/finance.
adan-legal: (typo corrected) dan-legal: I'll push the addendum tonight and email m.singh. Jess, can you get the SOW skeleton and the pilot commercial terms?
jess-partnerships: will send SOW template and pilot headcount estimates in next 2 hours and loop sales.
lee-procurement: summary of next steps: 1) Dan: draft addendum for pass-through/subcontractor model. 2) Jess: SOW + pilot terms. 3) Lee/Marco: provide DUNS/VAT/W9 docs. 4) Atlas legal reviews + countersign. 5) Olivia: ops to coordinate manual marketplace submission under Redwood account.
marco-finance: noted. If addendum signed and VAT confirmed, finance can accept invoicing Atlas.
jess-partnerships: thanks team. tagging @sarah-sales for visibility. If we get countersign by EOD tomorrow we can aim to push the marketplace transaction by Thursday.
lee-procurement: i'll monitor. please paste any signatures here when available. :thumbsup:
